items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Teddy Wilson's orchestra had Adolphus "Doc" Cheatham, Carl(Baura) George and Harold "Shorty" Baker in the trumpet section... The only ones in this band that were not new to me were "Doc" Cheatham... and of course, Teddy.

ctx.x: The Coleman Hawkin's orchestra was composed of Joe Guy and Tommy Lindsay, trumpets, Earl Hardy, trombone, Eustice Moore, Jackie Fields, altos, Ernie Powell, tenor, Gene Rodgers, piano, Charles Smith, bass, Arthur Herbert, drums and Thelma Carpenter, vocalist. The only musicians in the band that I had known before going to Europe were Jackie Fields and Gene Rodgers.

Teddy Wilson's orchestra had Adolphus "Doc" Cheatham, Carl(Baura) George and Harold "Shorty" Baker in the trumpet section. Jake Wiley, Floyd "Stumpy" Brady, trombone, Rudy Powell, alto & clarinet, Pete Clark, alto & baritone, George Irish and Bob Carroll, tenor, Al Casey, guitar, Al Hall, bass, J.C. Heard, drums, and Jean Eldridge, Vocals. Buster Harding was arranger and second or stand-in pianist. The only ones in this band that were not new to me were "Doc" Cheatham, "Stumpy", Brady, Rudy Powell, Pete Clark,…

One of the first things I had to do upon my return to New York was to be registered in the musicians union because I had let it drop in 1936. It costed me fifty dollars. There was a union in Paris, France, but hardly any musicians belonged to it.
